title: Default Passwords
description: A profile has a default password when the profile's password matches the user profile name. A change was made in 7.5 so that the default for the password on CRTUSRPRF is *NONE. When you create new user profiles, consider assigning a unique, non-trivial password instead of using a default password. Default passwords provide an opportunity for someone to enter your system anonymously. Default passwords are easy to guess. Additionally, accounts with default passwords are often used for shared (non-unique) accounts.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.6 Default Passwords

audit.command: On a command line, type STRSQL and press Enter Enter the following SQL statement and press Enter. SELECT ALL USER_NAME, STATUS, DFTPWD, PWDEXP FROM QSYS2/USER_INFO T01 WHERE DFTPWD = 'YES'

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, change the password of all user profiles with default passwords to a non-trivial password and set the password to expire. CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) PASSWORD(<xxxxxx>) PWDEXP(*YES) Additionally, the command ANZDFTPWD ACTION (*DISABLE) should be added to a job schedule entry to periodically scan for and *DISABLE any profiles with *DEFAULT passwords, and system value QPWDRULES should contain the parameters *ALLCRTCHG and *LMTPRFNAME to prevent the creation of profiles with *DEFAULT passwords.

title: QSECOFR Profile Shall Be *DISABLED
description: The QSECOFR profile shall be *DISABLED to prevent interactive use. You can always sign on with the QSECOFR profile at the console, even if the status of QSECOFR is *DISABLED. QSECOFR is the most powerful profile on the IBM i and is equivalent to the UNIX Root Profile. Additionally, you should prevent QSECOFR from interactively signing on by *DISABLING it and create unique security officer profiles as required by the business.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.1 QSECOFR Profile Shall Be *DISABLED

audit.command: DSPUSRPRF USRPRF(QSECOFR) Observe the Status to ensure that it is *DISABLED

remediation.command: CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(QSECOFR) STATUS(*DISABLED)

title: Administrative Special Authorities
description: Special authority is used to specify the types of actions a user can perform on system resources. A system administrator can be given one or more special authorities directly or through a group. System administrators should be granted administrative special authorities commensurate with their job roles.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.4 Administrative Special Authorities

audit.command: PRTUSRPRF SELECT(*SPCAUT) SPCAUT(*ALL) Type WRKSPLF and locate your spool file with the name QPSECUSR and User Data PRTUSRPRF. View the spool file output to ensure that all administrators listed with Special Authorities have the least privileges commensurate with their administrative job roles. Note that administrative Special Authorities are cumulative from User Profile and Group Profiles. IBM supplied user profiles will appear in the report and should be excluded from the audit. A list of IBM supplied user profiles can be obtained from the references below.

remediation.command: Special authority is a type of authority a user can have to perform system functions, including all object authority, save system authority, job control authority, security administrator authority, spool control authority, service authority, and system configuration authority. To establish the recommended configuration, lower all administrators to the special authorities commensurate with their job roles. CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) SPCAUT(<xxxxxx>) Change all non-administrative *USER class users and groups to SPCAUT = *NONE: CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) SPCAUT(*NONE)

title: User Profile With Non-Expiring Passwords
description: User Profiles with non-expiring passwords are never required to change their password. Non-expiring passwords are security risks because if no automated solution is in place, users are never prompted to change their passwords.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.8 User Profile With Non-Expiring Passwords

audit.command: On a command line, type STRSQL and press Enter Enter the following SQL statement and press Enter. SELECT ALL USER_NAME, STATUS, PWDEXPITV, LASTUSED FROM QSYS2/USER_INFO T01 WHERE PWDEXPITV = -1 AND NOPWD ='NO' Service accounts may be excluded from the audit and remediation. A service account is a user account that is created explicitly to provide a security context for automated system and application services running on the system. Service accounts should be configured with a non-trivial, complex password that is used in an automated service process and ... (full steps: CIS section 4.8)

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, change all interactive user profile password expiration intervals to *SYSVAL. Note: Service profiles may be set to a non-expiring password (*NOMAX) commensurate with your organization policy. CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) PWDEXPITV(*SYSVAL)

title: Group Profiles With Passwords
description: Group profiles should not have a password as they are usually not associated with a unique account. Unique accounts provide accountability to the actions they perform.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.11 Group Profiles With Passwords

audit.command: On a command line, type STRSQL and press Enter Copy or type the following SQL statement to the terminal and press Enter. SELECT All T01.GROUPNAME, T02.NOPWD FROM QSYS2/GROUPLIST T01 INNER JOIN QSYS2/USER_INFO T02 ON T01.GROUPNAME = T02.USER_NAME WHERE T02.NOPWD = 'NO' Verify that the display returns no group profiles with a password (NOPWD = NO).

remediation.command: CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) PASSWORD(*NONE) Where USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) in the above example is the group profile/s from the above audit.

title: Implement Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
description: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a layered approach to securing physical and logical access where a system requires a user to present a combination of two or more different authenticators to verify a user's identity for login. Adversaries are increasingly capable of guessing or harvesting passwords to gain illicit access. Password cracking techniques are becoming more sophisticated and high- powered computing is increasingly affordable.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.12 Implement Multi-factor authentication (MFA)

audit.command: IBM and third-party vendors provide MFA solutions for IBM i, and organizations often choose to buy and implement one of these solutions or develop an in-house MFA solution. The business should provide implementation details from the vendor or in- house solution to provide an adequate audit procedure.

remediation.command: Evaluate 3rd party MFA solutions available from various vendors or develop an in- house MFA solution.

title: Set Block Password Change
description: Specifies the time period during which a password is blocked from being changed following the prior successful password change operation. This system value does not restrict password changes made by the Change User Profile (CHGUSRPRF) command. By restricting the frequency of password changes, an administrator can prevent users from repeatedly changing their password in an attempt to circumvent password reuse controls.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.21 Set Block Password Change

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDCHGBLK) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDCHGBLK) and verify the value is "24". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDCHGBLK) VALUE('24')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "24": QPWDCHGBLK CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDCHGBLK) VALUE('24')

title: Set Password Expiration Interval
description: Determines the maximum number of days a password is valid from 1 to 366 or *NOMAX. Note that service accounts may have their PWDEXPITV set to *NOMAX on the user profile whereas standard user profiles should be set to *SYSVAL. This helps to prevent access to unauthorized persons by forcing a password change after a set number of days.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.22 Set Password Expiration Interval

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDEXPITV) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDEXPITV) and verify the value is "45". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDEXPITV) VALUE('45')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "45": QPWDEXPITV CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDEXPITV) VALUE('45')

title: Set Password Level
description: Determines the length of password that is supported as well as removing weak and deprecated NTLM passwords for Windows 95/98/ME clients from the system. User passwords with a length of 1-128 characters are supported and exclude the use of decryptable password hashes (NTLM) for older 16-bit clients. This provides additional security by having options to only support passwords that meets specified length and security requirements.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.24 Set Password Level

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDLVL) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDLVL) and verify the value is "4". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDLVL) VALUE(4)

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "4": QPWDLVL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDLVL) VALUE(4)

title: Set Required Difference in Passwords
description: This policy setting determines the number of renewed, unique passwords that have to be associated with a user account before you can reuse an old password. To maintain the effectiveness of this policy setting, use the Block Password Change (QPWDCHGBLK) setting to prevent users from repeatedly changing their password.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.25 Set Required Difference in Passwords

audit.command: DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRQDDIF). Ensure that QPWDRQDDIF is set to a value of 2=Cannot be the same as last 24.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "2": QPWDRQDDIF CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRQDDIF) VALUE('2')

title: Set Password Rules
description: Specifies the rules used to check whether a password is formed correctly. This provides additional security by having a system in place to verify if a password meets the specified rules set.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.26 Set Password Rules

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDRULES) and verify the value is the value set by CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) VALUE('*ALLCRTCHG *DGTLMTAJC *DGTLMTFST *DGTLMTLST *LMTPRFNAME *MAXLEN10 *MINLEN8 *REQANY3 *SPCCHRLMTAJC *SPCCHRLMTFST *SPCCHRLMTLST'). Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) VALUE('*ALLCRTCHG *DGTLMTAJC *DGTLMTFST *DGTLMTLST *LMTPRFNAME *MAXLEN10 *MINLEN8 *REQANY3 *SPCCHRLMTAJC *SPCCHRLMTFST *SPCCHRLMTLST')

remediation.command: CALL QCMD CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) VALUE('*ALLCRTCHG *DGTLMTAJC *DGTLMTFST *DGTLMTLST *LMTPRFNAME *MAXLEN10 *MINLEN8 *REQANY3 *SPCCHRLMTAJC *SPCCHRLMTFST *SPCCHRLMTLST')

title: Set Secure Sockets Layer Cipher Specification List
description: Specifies the list of cipher suites that are supported by System. The values are read- only unless the QSSLCSLCTL (cipher control) system value is set to *USRDFN. Configuring your IBM i server to allow the use of weak protocols and weak cipher suites will result in your IBM i server potentially being at risk of a network security breach.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.35 Set Secure Sockets Layer Cipher Specification List

audit.command: DSPSYSVAL QSSLCSL

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *OPSYS: QSSLCSLCTL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSSLCSLCTL) VALUE('*OPSYS')

title: Set Secure Sockets Layer Cipher Control
description: Specifies whether or not the QSSLCSL (cipher specification list) system value is controlled by the system or by the user. Configuring your IBM i server to allow the use of weak protocols and weak cipher suites will result in your IBM i server potentially being at risk of a network security breach.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.36 Set Secure Sockets Layer Cipher Control

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSSLCSLCTL) (or WRKSYSVAL QSSLCSLCTL) and verify the value is *OPSYS. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSSLCSLCTL) VALUE('*OPSYS')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *OPSYS: QSSLCSLCTL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSSLCSLCTL) VALUE('*OPSYS')

title: Set Block Password Change
description: Specifies the time period during which a password is blocked from being changed following the prior successful password change operation. This system value does not restrict password changes made by the Change User Profile (CHGUSRPRF) command. By restricting the frequency of password changes, an administrator can prevent users from repeatedly changing their password in an attempt to circumvent password reuse controls.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.17 Set Block Password Change

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDCHGBLK) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDCHGBLK) and verify the value is "99". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDCHGBLK) VALUE('99')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "99": QPWDCHGBLK CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDCHGBLK) VALUE('99')

title: Set Password Expiration Interval
description: Determines the maximum number of days a password is valid from 1 to 366 or *NOMAX. Note that service accounts may have their PWDEXPITV set to *NOMAX on the user profile whereas standard user profiles should be set to *SYSVAL. This helps to prevent access to unauthorized persons by promoting longer passphrases that are more difficult to crack.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.18 Set Password Expiration Interval

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDEXPITV) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDEXPITV) and verify the value is "365". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDEXPITV) VALUE('365')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "365": QPWDEXPITV CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDEXPITV) VALUE('365')

title: Set Required Difference in Passwords
description: Specifies a code that determines how many of the most recent prior passwords are not allowed. This value provides additional security by preventing users from specifying passwords that were used previously. It also prevents a user whose password has expired from changing it and then immediately changing it back to the old password.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.19 Set Required Difference in Passwords

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRQDDIF) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDRQDDIF) and verify the value is "1". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRQDDIF) VALUE('1')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "1": QPWDRQDDIF CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRQDDIF) VALUE('1')

title: Set Password Rules
description: Specifies the rules used to check whether a password is formed correctly. This provides additional security by having a system in place to verify if a password meets the specified rules set.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.20 Set Password Rules

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) (or WRKSYSVAL QPWDRULES) and verify the value is the value set by CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) VALUE('*ALLCRTCHG *LMTPRFNAME *MAXLEN128 *MINLEN14 *REQANY3'). Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) VALUE('*ALLCRTCHG *LMTPRFNAME *MAXLEN128 *MINLEN14 *REQANY3')

remediation.command: CALL QCMD CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDRULES) VALUE('*ALLCRTCHG *LMTPRFNAME *MAXLEN128 *MINLEN14 *REQANY3')

title: Set Password Validation Program
description: This provides the ability for a user-written program to do additional validation on passwords. This provides additional security by using the programs to do additional checking of user-assigned passwords before they are accepted by the system.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.21 Set Password Validation Program

audit.command: DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDVLDPGM) Ensure that the value specified the name of a Password Validation Program or *REGFAC.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, create a password validation program and set the following system value to either a value of the name of your program and library or *REGFAC: QPWDVLDPGM CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QPWDVLDPGM) VALUE(<pgmxxx libxxx>) Note that if using a value of *REGFAC, you must also register the program to the QIBM_QSY_VLD_PASSWRD exit point, format VLDP0200. ADDEXITPGM EXITPNT(QIBM_QSY_VLD_PASSWRD) FORMAT(VLDP0200) PGMNBR(*HIGH) PGM(<libxxx/pgmxxx>) See the References for additional information.

title: Exit Points
description: The IBM i provides several host servers and related objects that are common for the IBM® i Access family. For each Host server, IBM provides one or more exit points to control the activity of the host server. The registration facility (WRKREGINF) shows information about IBM® i exit points and their associated exit programs.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.7 Exit Points

audit.command: On a command line, type STRSQL and press Enter Copy or type the following SQL statement to the terminal and press Enter. SELECT T01.EXIT_NAME, T01.EXIT_FMT, T01.REGISTERED, T01.EXIT_PGMS, T02.NUMBER, T02.LIBRARY, T02."PROGRAM", T02.TEXT FROM QSYS2/EXIT_POINT T01 LEFT OUTER JOIN QSYS2/EXIT_PGM T02 ON T01.EXIT_NAME = T02.EXIT_NAME WHERE T01.EXIT_NAME LIKE 'QIBM_QTMF%' OR T01.EXIT_NAME LIKE 'QIBM_QZRC_RMT%' OR T01.EXIT_NAME LIKE 'QIBM_QMF_MESSAGE%' OR T01.EXIT_NAME LIKE 'QIBM_QZDA%' OR T01.EXIT_NAME LIKE 'QIBM_QZRC%' OR T01.EXIT_NAME LIKE 'QIBM_QDB_OPEN%' OR ... (full steps: CIS section 5.2.7)

remediation.command: Write or purchase user exit programs and register to associated exit points using the WRKREGINF and ADDEXITPGM commands.

title: Telnet Protocol
description: Restrict Telnet to SSL only to prevent sniffing of clear text passwords. Allowing the use of clear-text passwords permits credentials to be intercepted over the network by sniffers, packet monitoring and communication trace tools which could easily lead to unauthorized access to system resources.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.10 Telnet Protocol

audit.command: Type command CHGTELNA and press F4. Ensure that the Allow Secure Socket Layer is set to *ONLY.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, change telnet to use SSL only: CHGTELNA ALWSSL(*ONLY)

title: FTP Protocol
description: Restrict FTP to SSL only to prevent sniffing of clear text passwords. Allowing the use of clear-text passwords permits credentials to be intercepted over the network by sniffers, packet monitoring and communication trace tools which could easily lead to unauthorized access to system resources.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.11 FTP Protocol

audit.command: Type command CHGFTPA and press F4. Ensure that the Allow Secure Socket Layer is set to *ONLY.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, change FTP to use SSL only: CHGFTPA ALWSSL(*ONLY)

title: IBM i NetServer LANMAN Password Hash
description: The underlying system LANMAN hash was removed in 7.5. The NetServer LANMAN setting is obsolete and no longer used regardless of the setting.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.3.2 IBM i NetServer LANMAN Password Hash

audit.command: Verify the configuration described in CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 section 5.3.2: The underlying system LANMAN hash was removed in 7.5. The NetServer LANMAN setting is obsolete and no longer used regardless of the setting.

remediation.command: Apply the remediation in CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 section 5.3.2.

title: Configuring SSH - disallow host based authentication
description: The recommendation is to edit the /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd_config file to ensure that host- based authentication is disallowed. Using host-based authentication, any user on a trusted host can log into another host on which this feature is enabled. Since this feature depends only on system authentication and not on user authentication, it must be disabled.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.4.3 Configuring SSH - disallow host based authentication

audit.command: DSPF '/QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd_config' On the Control field, type HostbasedAuthentication and press F16 (shift F4) Control: HostbasedAuthentication___________________________________ The display should yield the following output: HostbasedAuthentication no

remediation.command: EDTF '/QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd_config' file to ensure that host based authentication is disallowed: Replace: #HostbasedAuthentication no With: HostbasedAuthentication no Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes:

title: Configuring SSH - set privilege separation
description: The recommendation is to edit the /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd_config file to ensure that privilege separation is enabled. Note, that as of OpenSSH 7.5 this configuration directive has been deprecated. Setting privilege separation helps to secure remote ssh access. Once a user is authenticated the sshd daemon creates a child process which has the privileges of the authenticated user and this then handles incoming network traffic.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.4.4 Configuring SSH - set privilege separation

audit.command: DSPF '/QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd_config' On the Control field, type UsePrivilegeSeparation and press F16 (shift F4) Control: UsePrivilegeSeparation __________________________________ The display should yield the following output: UsePrivilegeSeparation yes

remediation.command: EDTF '/QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd_config' file to ensure that privilege separation is enabled: Replace: UsePrivilegeSeparation no With: UsePrivilegeSeparation yes Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes: Note: In IBM i OpenSSH 6.9p1, UsePrivilegeSeparation is explicitly set to "no". Once upgrading to 8.0p1, UsePrivilegeSeparation is deprecated. There is a warning message generated when the sshd server is started when the option exists in sshd_config. To disable the warning, you can comment out or remove the line containing UsePrivilegeSeparation from the sshd_config file.

title: Configuring SSH - restrict Cipher list
description: This variable limits the types of ciphers that SSH can use during communication. Based on research conducted at various institutions, it was determined that the symmetric portion of the SSH Transport Protocol (as described in RFC 4253) has security weaknesses that allowed recovery of up to 32 bits of plaintext from a block of ...
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.4.7 Configuring SSH - restrict Cipher list

audit.command: DSPF '/QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd_config' On the Control field, type Ciphers and press F16 (shift F4) Control: Ciphers_________________________________________ The display should yield the following output: Ciphers aes256-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes128-ctr

remediation.command: EDTF '/QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/sshd'_config file: Insert: Ciphers aes256-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes128-ctr Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes:

title: System Service Tools Password Expiration Interval
description: Numerous studies had found that excessive password expiration requirements do more harm than good, because these requirements make users select predictable passwords, composed of sequential words and numbers that are closely related to each other. This helps to prevent access to unauthorized persons by promoting longer passphrases that are more difficult to crack.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.1 System Service Tools Password Expiration Interval

audit.command: On a command line type DSPSSTSECA and press ENTER Verify that the Service tools password expiration interval is 365.

remediation.command: To change the default password expiration interval from 180 days, follow these steps. CHGSSTSECA REQUSRID(<xxxxxx>) REQPWD(<xxxxxx>) PWDEXPITV(365)

title: System Service Tools Changing the duplicate password control
description: This policy setting determines the duplicate password control. The recommended state for this setting is: 18 The longer a user uses the same password, the greater the chance that an attacker can determine the password through brute force attacks. Also, any accounts that may have been compromised will remain exploitable for as long as the password is left unchanged.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.3 System Service Tools Changing the duplicate password control

audit.command: On a command line type DSPSSTSECA and press ENTER Verify that the Service Duplicate password control is set to 18

remediation.command: To change the default duplicate password control, complete these steps. CHGSSTSECA REQUSRID(<xxxxxx>) REQPWD(<xxxxxx>) DUPPWDCTL(18)

title: System Service Tools Password Level
description: This policy setting determines the password level for System Service Tools. SST Password level 3 includes password-based Key Derivation Function 2 (PBKDF2) with HMAC SHA512 (SHA-2 512 bit) encryption The recommended state for this setting is: PWLVL 3 The default password level (PWLVL 2) uses deprecated SHA encryption. To change to use HMAC SHA512 encryption, the System Service Tools Password Level should be set to PWLVL 3 for better security.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.4 System Service Tools Password Level

audit.command: On a command line type DSPSSTSECA and press ENTER Verify that the Service tools password level is 3

remediation.command: To change the service tools password level. CHGSSTSECA REQUSRID(<xxxxxx>) REQPWD(<xxxxxx>) SSTPWDLVL(3)

title: System Service Tools IDs and Privileges
description: This policy setting determines the functional privileges of System Service Tool Users. All System Service Tools Users are powerful administrators. Service Tools Users should follow the same policy as Operating System Users.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.6 System Service Tools IDs and Privileges

audit.command: 1. Type DSPSSTUSR and press Enter. 2. Review the screen output information with your system administrator and ensure that all SST users have unique profiles. Do not use the shipped IBM User IDs. 3. Ensure that all Service Tools IDs have the proper functional privileges for their job roles.

remediation.command: Disable/Remove default and inactive IDs and ensure that each ID has the required privileges. Ensure that each unique SST ID has privileges commensurate with the Principle of Least Privilege for each unique job role.

title: System Service Tools Password Rules
description: Specifies the rules used to check whether a password is formed correctly. This provides additional security by having a system in place to verify if a password meets the specified rules set.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.8 System Service Tools Password Rules

audit.command: From a command line type DSPSSTSECA and press Enter Verify the following Password Rules are set: 1. Limit profile name is *YES 2. Hours to block password change is 24 3. Minimum password length is 14 4. Maximum password length is 128 5. Use characters from three groups is *YES 6. Minimum digits is 1 7. Limit adjacent digits is *NO 8. Limit digit first position is *NO 9. Limit digit last position is *NO 10. Limit adjacent special characters is *NO 11. Limit special character first position is *NO 12. Limit special character last position is *NO

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set SST Password Rules with the following command: CHGSSTSECA PWDRULES(*YES 24 14 128 *YES *NO *NO *NO 1 *NOMAX *NO *NO *NO *NONE *NOMAX *NO *NO *NO *NONE *NONE *NOMAX *NO *NO *NO)

title: System Service Tools Allow add and remove of password exit programs
description: Controls the ability of system administrators to add or remove a registered password exit program. This provides additional security by having a control in place to prevent system administrator's ability to add or remove a password exit program.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.9 System Service Tools Allow add and remove of password exit programs

audit.command: From a command line type DSPSSTSECA and press Enter Verify that the Allow add and remove of password exit program is set to *NO

remediation.command: To change the service tools Add and remove pwd exit pgms value. CHGSSTSECA REQUSRID() REQPWD() PWDEXITPGM(*NO)

title: QSECOFR Shall Not be Configured as a Group Profile
description: QSECOFR shall not be a group profile as this would allow group members to inherit root privileges from the shipped IBM QSECOFR profile. Do not use IBM profiles as groups. Instead, create your own group profiles with appropriate privileges (special authorities) commensurate with your job roles and the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP).
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.2 QSECOFR Shall Not be Configured as a Group Profile

title: User Profile Action Auditing
description: This subcategory reports when a user account or service uses a sensitive privilege. Auditing these events may be useful when investigating a security incident. The CHGUSRAUD (Change User Audit) command allows a user with audit (*AUDIT) special authority to set up or change auditing for a user.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.5 User Profile Action Auditing

audit.command: PRTUSRPRF SELECT(*SPCAUT) SPCAUT(*ALL) Type WRKSPLF to locate your spool file with the name QPSECUSR and User Data PRTUSRPRF. Note that administrative Special Authorities are cumulative from User Profile and Group Profiles. IBM supplied user profiles with the exception of QSECOFR should be excluded from the audit. description: Remove/disable inactive user profiles within 90 days. Accounts that are not used regularly are often targets of attack since it is less likely that any changes (such as a changed password) will be noticed. As such, these accounts may be more easily exploited and used to access sensitive data.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.7 Inactive Profiles

audit.command: On a command line, type STRSQL and press Enter Enter the following SQL statement and press Enter. SELECT USER_NAME, STATUS, LASTUSED, TIMESTAMP FROM QSYS2/USER_INFO T01 WHERE STATUS = '*ENABLED' AND LASTUSED <= 'yyyy-mm-dd' AND TIMESTAMP <= 'yyyy-mm-dd' OR STATUS = '*ENABLED' AND TIMESTAMP <= 'yyyy-mm-dd' AND LASTUSED IS NULL Note: In the above SQL, enter the calendar date equal to 90 days prior to the audit or that of your inactive profile policy as the LASTUSED date in the format yyyy-mm-dd. The date needs to be entered in 'yyyy-mm-dd' format enclosed in ... (full steps: CIS section 4.7)

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, remove/disable all inactive profiles displayed. CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) STATUS(*DISABLED) Optional (recommended) on a regular basis such as 30-90 days after inactive profiles have been *DISABLED, they should be archived and removed. DLTUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) Note that when removing user profiles, there needs to be consideration of changing ownership of the objects they own.

title: User Profiles With Command Line Access
description: User Profiles with command line access can run commands they are authorized to from a command line. Application user profiles should be limited to menus and restricted from directly running system commands from a command line.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.9 User Profiles With Command Line Access

audit.command: On a command line, type STRSQL and press Enter Enter the following SQL statement and press Enter. SELECT ALL USER_NAME, STATUS, LMTCPB, SPCAUT FROM QSYS2/USER_INFO T01 WHERE LMTCPB <> '*YES' IBM supplied user profiles will appear in the report and should be excluded from the audit. A list of IBM supplied user profiles can be obtained from the references below.

description: This section contains information about the IBM-supplied user profiles that are shipped with the system and Licensed Program Products. These profiles are used as object owners for various system functions. Some system functions also run under specific IBM-supplied user profiles. You must change the password for the QSECOFR profile after you install your system. This password is the same for every IBM i system and poses a security exposure until it is changed. However, do not change any other values for IBM-supplied user profiles.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.10 IBM Supplied User Profiles

CHGUSRPRF USRPRF(<xxxxxx>) GRPPRF(<xxxxxx>) SUPGRPPRF(<xxxxxx>) Note: Many of the IBM-supplied user profiles cannot be specified on CHGUSRPRF. title: Set Allow Restoration of Security-Sensitive Objects
description: Determines if the system will allow authorized users to restore system-state objects or programs that adopt authority to the system. System administrators must use this privileged access to restore objects frequently as a part of their routine IBM-supplied PTF O/S maintenance as well as related to back-up and recovery processes for applications.

title: Set Attention Program
description: Determines what program is executed when the user presses the Attention key. (Note:*ASSIST is interpreted by the system to use the QSYS/QEZMAIN program, which is displayed if you view the setting using the PRTSYSSECA command.) You can specify the program to call when you press the Attention key.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.2 Set Attention Program

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QATNPGM) (or WRKSYSVAL QATNPGM) and verify the value is *NONE. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QATNPGM) VALUE('*NONE')

description: Serves as the on/off switch for security auditing. *AUDLVL activates event auditing at the system or user level. *OBJAUD activates object auditing. *NOQTEMP prevents extraneous auditing entries for objects in library QTEMP. Auditing can be defined as an inspection or examination of a process or system to determine the quality of it, and is also used to ensure compliance to requirements.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.3 Set Auditing Control

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDCTL) (or WRKSYSVAL QAUDCTL) and verify the value is *NOQTEMP, *OBJAUD, *AUDLVL. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDCTL) VALUE('*NOQTEMP *OBJAUD *AUDLVL')

title: Set Auditing End Action
description: Determines the action the system should take if it is unable to continue auditing (e.g. the audit record is full). System continues to operate but sends a message to the system operator and to the QSYS/QSYSMSG of the message.

description: Specifies the interval in minutes that a job can be disconnected before the system ends the job. A disconnected job uses up system resources, as well as retaining any locks on objects and should be ended eventually to avoid this.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "0": QRMTSRVATR CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QRMTSRVATR) VALUE('0')

title: Set Scan File System
description: Specifies the integrated file system in which objects will be scanned when exit programs are registered with any of the integrated file system scan-related exit points. This provides an additional layer of security because this option can be used to scan for a virus.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.31 Set Scan File System

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSCANFS) (or WRKSYSVAL QSCANFS) and verify the value is *ROOTOPNUD. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSCANFS) VALUE('*ROOTOPNUD')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *ROOTOPNUD: QSCANFS CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSCANFS) VALUE('*ROOTOPNUD')

title: Set Scan File System Control
description: Controls the integrated file system scanning on the system when exit programs are registered with any of the integrated file system scan-related exit points. This ensures that any failure from the scan exit programs prevents the associated operations, and also disallows the exit program additional access levels.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.32 Set Scan File System Control

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSCANFSCTL) (or WRKSYSVAL QSCANFSCTL) and verify the value is *ERRFAIL and *NOWRTUPG. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSCANFSCTL) VALUE('*ERRFAIL *NOWRTUPG')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *ERRFAIL and *NOWRTUPG: QSCANFSCTL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSCANFSCTL) VALUE('*ERRFAIL *NOWRTUPG')

title: Set System Security Level
description: Determines the level of security features supported. Level 40 is the recommend level of security for non-DoD production systems. In addition to password authentication and privileged access controls, level 40 can effectively safeguard data, programs, and other production objects and prevent unintentional data loss or modification.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.33 Set System Security Level

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSECURITY) (or WRKSYSVAL QSECURITY) and verify the value is "40". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSECURITY) VALUE('40')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "40": QSECURITY CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSECURITY) VALUE('40')

title: Set Shared Memory Control
description: Controls whether or not users are allowed to use shared memory APIs or mapped memory objects that have write capability to modify shared memory.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.34 Set Shared Memory Control

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSHRMEMCTL) (or WRKSYSVAL QSHRMEMCTL) and verify the value is "1". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSHRMEMCTL) VALUE('1')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following value to "1": QSHRMEMCTL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSHRMEMCTL) VALUE('1')

title: Set Secure Socket Layer Security Protocols
description: Specifies the SSL protocol versions supported by System SSL. Configuring your IBM i server to allow the use of weak protocols and weak cipher suites will result in your IBM i server potentially being at risk of a network security breach.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.37 Set Secure Socket Layer Security Protocols

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSSLPCL) (or WRKSYSVAL QSSLPCL) and verify the value is *OPSYS.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *OPSYS: QSSLPCL CHGSYSVAL QSSLPCL VALUE('*OPSYS')

title: Set System Library List
description: The system library list (QSYSLIBL) system value is used as the first part of the library list associated with a job. The libraries in the system part of the library list of a job are searched before any other libraries in the library list of a job. The list can contain as many as 15 names. The security of the System Library List is a vital part of your overall system security. All libraries in the System Library List should provide *PUBLIC *USE authority.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.38 Set System Library List

audit.command: DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSYSLIBL) Make note of all Libraries in the System part of the library list DSPOBJAUT OBJ(<xxxxxx>) OBJTYPE(*LIB) For each library in the list Ensure that each library in the list grants *PUBLIC *USE Object Authority and that any additional Users with an authority greater than *USE are properly authorized by the business to introduce changes into the library.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the *PUBLIC authority to *USE to all libraries in the System part of the library list QSYSLIBL that grant an authority greater than *USE: GRTOBJAUT OBJ(<xxxxxx>) OBJTYPE(*LIB) USER(*PUBLIC) AUT(*USE) REPLACE(*YES)

title: Set Use Adopted Authority
description: Controls those users allowed to create or change programs that use adopted authority from other programs that call it. If an authorization list is specified, *PUBLIC(EXCLUDE) should be used.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.39 Set Use Adopted Authority

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QUSEADPAUT) (or WRKSYSVAL QUSEADPAUT) and verify the value is the value set by CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QUSEADPAUT) VALUE(QUSEADPAUT). Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QUSEADPAUT) VALUE(QUSEADPAUT)

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, enter a name for the authorization list for the following system value: QUSEADPAUT CRTAUTL AUTL(QUSEADPAUT) AUT(*EXCLUDE) CHGOBJOWN OBJ(QUSEADPAUT) OBJTYPE(*AUTL) NEWOWN(QSYS) CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QUSEADPAUT) VALUE(QUSEADPAUT)

title: Set Verify Object On Restore
description: Determines when signatures will be verified and if the object will be restored without a valid signature. (See also QALWOBJRST & QFRCCVNRST, 2.1.1.1 and 2.1.1.16) Use this value for normal operations, when you expect some of the objects you restore to be unsigned, but you want to ensure that all signed objects have signatures that are valid.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1.40 Set Verify Object On Restore

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QVFYOBJRST) (or WRKSYSVAL QVFYOBJRST) and verify the value is "3". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QVFYOBJRST) VALUE('3')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "3": QVFYOBJRST CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QVFYOBJRST) VALUE('3')

title: Set Allow Restoration of Security-Sensitive Objects
description: Does not allow objects with security-sensitive attributes to be restored. Because some programs may cause serious problems, this system value provides a method to protect your system.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.1 Set Allow Restoration of Security-Sensitive Objects

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QALWOBJRST) (or WRKSYSVAL QALWOBJRST) and verify the value is *NONE. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QALWOBJRST) VALUE('*NONE')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *NONE: QALWOBJRST CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QALWOBJRST) VALUE('*NONE')

title: Set Allow User Domain Objects in These Libraries
description: This specifies the names of the libraries that can contain the *USRSPC (user space), *USRIDX (user index), and *USRQ (user queue) type objects. In our environment many vendor applications are making use of USRxx objects in numerous and changing libraries. Some systems have application software that relies on object types *USRSPC, *USRIDX, or *USRQ. For those systems, the list of libraries for the QALWUSRDMN system value should include the libraries that are used by the application software.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.2 Set Allow User Domain Objects in These Libraries

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QALWUSRDMN) (or WRKSYSVAL QALWUSRDMN) and verify the value is QTEMP. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QALWUSRDMN) VALUE('QTEMP')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to QTEMP: QALWUSRDMN CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QALWUSRDMN) VALUE('QTEMP')

title: Set Auditing Control
description: Serves as the on/off switch for security auditing. *AUDLVL activates event auditing at the system or user level. *OBJAUD activates object auditing. *NOQTEMP prevents extraneous auditing entries for objects in library QTEMP. Auditing can be defined as an inspection or examination of a process or system to determine the quality of it, and is also used to ensure compliance to requirements. Activates event and object auditing including QTEMP
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.3 Set Auditing Control

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDCTL) (or WRKSYSVAL QAUDCTL) and verify the value is *OBJAUD, *AUDLVL. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDCTL) VALUE('*OBJAUD *AUDLVL')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *OBJAUD, *AUDLVL : QAUDCTL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDCTL) VALUE('*OBJAUD *AUDLVL')

title: Set Auditing End Action
description: Determines the action the system should take if it is unable to continue auditing (e.g. the audit record is full). If the system is unable to write audit journal entries and the QAUDENDACN system value is *PWRDWNSYS, your system ends abnormally. This might cause a lengthy initial program load (IPL) when your system is powered on again.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.4 Set Auditing End Action

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDENDACN) (or WRKSYSVAL QAUDENDACN) and verify the value is *PWRDWNSYS. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDENDACN) VALUE('*PWRDWNSYS')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *PWRDWNSYS: QAUDENDACN CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDENDACN) VALUE('*PWRDWNSYS')

title: Set Auditing Force Level
description: Determines how many auditing journal entries records are cached in memory before they are physically written to disk from memory. This will provide the best auditing performance.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.5 Set Auditing Force Level

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDFRCLVL) (or WRKSYSVAL QAUDFRCLVL) and verify the value is "1". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDFRCLVL) VALUE(1)

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "1": QAUDFRCLVL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUDFRCLVL) VALUE(1)

title: Set Automatic Virtual Device Creation
description: Determines whether automatic device creation is allowed and if so, how many devices can be configured automatically. 32500 is the maximum numerical value that can be set for this system value and is both sufficient to support the needs of the business and not too large to represent a denial of service exposure since it represents a finite limit.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.6 Set Automatic Virtual Device Creation

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUTOVRT) (or WRKSYSVAL QAUTOVRT) and verify the value is "0". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUTOVRT) VALUE(0)

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "0": QAUTOVRT CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QAUTOVRT) VALUE(0)

title: Set Create Authority
description: Specifies the default public authority. Sets *EXCLUDE as the default public authority for new objects created in libraries that do not have a CRTAUT value specified. This excludes the public from newly created objects. This will ensure the integrity of the newly created objects. You can override the QCRTAUT system value at a library level to specify data classifications within specific application libraries.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.7 Set Create Authority

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QCRTAUT) (or WRKSYSVAL QCRTAUT) and verify the value is *EXCLUDE. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QCRTAUT) VALUE('*EXCLUDE')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *EXCLUDE: QCRTAUT CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QCRTAUT) VALUE('*EXCLUDE')

title: Set Create Object Audit Level
description: Determines the default object auditing level for new objects. An audit record is written for any security relevant action that affects the read or change of all newly created objects.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.8 Set Create Object Audit Level

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QCRTOBJAUD) (or WRKSYSVAL QCRTOBJAUD) and verify the value is *ALL. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QCRTOBJAUD) VALUE('*ALL')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *ALL: QCRTOBJAUD CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QCRTOBJAUD) VALUE('*ALL')

title: Set Disconnect-Job Interval
description: Specifies the interval in minutes that a job can be disconnected before the system ends the job. A disconnected job uses up system resources, as well as retaining any locks on objects, and should be ended eventually to avoid this.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.9 Set Disconnect-Job Interval

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QDSCJOBITV) (or WRKSYSVAL QDSCJOBITV) and verify the value is "15" (Times out disconnected jobs after 15 minutes). Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QDSCJOBITV) VALUE('15')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "15" (Times out disconnected jobs after 15 minutes): QDSCJOBITV CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QDSCJOBITV) VALUE('15')

title: Set Force Conversion On Restore
description: Determines under what conditions objects will be forced to convert when they are being restored to the system. When an object is translated it is recompiled using a trusted translator guaranteed not to circumvent the integrity of the system. (See also QALWOBJRST & QVFYOBJRST, 2.1.2.1 and 2.1.2.31) All objects will be converted.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.10 Set Force Conversion On Restore

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QFRCCVNRST) (or WRKSYSVAL QFRCCVNRST) and verify the value is "7". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QFRCCVNRST) VALUE('7')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "7": QFRCCVNRST CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QFRCCVNRST) VALUE('7')

title: Set Inactivity Time-out Interval
description: Determines the interval in minutes that a workstation can be inactive before the system sends a message to a message queue or ends the job. All users must use a password protected screen saver that locks the PC after 15 minutes of inactivity to comply with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.11 Set Inactivity Time-out Interval

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QINACTITV) (or WRKSYSVAL QINACTITV) and verify the value is "15" (The system times out inactive jobs after 15 minutes of inactivity). Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QINACTITV) VALUE('15')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "15" (The system times out inactive jobs after 15 minutes of inactivity): QINACTITV CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QINACTITV) VALUE('15')

title: Set Inactivity Message Queue
description: Specifies either the action to be taken when the inactivity time-out interval is reached or the name of the message queue that will receive messages about the workstation. The current system standard ends the job after the inactivity time-out interval is reached. Controlling inactive jobs provides security so that users do not leave signed on displays inactive.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.12 Set Inactivity Message Queue

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QINACTMSGQ) (or WRKSYSVAL QINACTMSGQ) and verify the value is *ENDJOB. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QINACTMSGQ) VALUE('*ENDJOB')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *ENDJOB: QINACTMSGQ CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QINACTMSGQ) VALUE('*ENDJOB')

title: Set Limit Device Sessions
description: Specifies if users can have concurrent device sessions. This is recommended because limiting users to a single device reduces the likelihood of sharing passwords and leaving devices unattended.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.13 Set Limit Device Sessions

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QLMTDEVSSN) (or WRKSYSVAL QLMTDEVSSN) and verify the value is '1'. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QLMTDEVSSN) VALUE('1')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to '1': QLMTDEVSSN CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QLMTDEVSSN) VALUE('1')

title: Set Limit Security Officer Access to Workstations
description: Limits users with *ALLOBJ or *SERVICE special authority to authorized devices. This system value controls whether users with *ALLOBJ or *SERVICE special authorities need explicit authority to specific work stations.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.14 Set Limit Security Officer Access to Workstations

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QLMTSECOFR) (or WRKSYSVAL QLMTSECOFR) and verify the value is "1". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QLMTSECOFR) VALUE('1')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "1": QLMTSECOFR CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QLMTSECOFR) VALUE('1')

title: Set Maximum Sign-on Action
description: Determines the action the system takes when a user reaches the maximum number of sign-on attempts. Disables the user profile and device when the maximum sign-on limit is reached. This disables the user profile when the number of incorrect sign-on attempts for the user reaches the value in the QMAXSIGN system value.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.15 Set Maximum Sign-on Action

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QMAXSGNACN) (or WRKSYSVAL QMAXSGNACN) and verify the value is "3". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QMAXSGNACN) VALUE('3')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "3": QMAXSGNACN CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QMAXSGNACN) VALUE('3')

title: Set Maximum Sign-on Attempts
description: Determines the maximum number of invalid sign-on attempts a user is allowed. This setting helps to prevent unauthorized access into user profiles by giving the user a limited number of login attempts before disabling the user profile
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.16 Set Maximum Sign-on Attempts

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QMAXSIGN) (or WRKSYSVAL QMAXSIGN) and verify the value is "3". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QMAXSIGN) VALUE('3')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "3": QMAXSIGN CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QMAXSIGN) VALUE('3')

title: Set Remote Sign-on Value
description: Determine whether and how automatic sign-on from a remote system is allowed.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.22 Set Remote Sign-on Value

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QRMTSIGN) (or WRKSYSVAL QRMTSIGN) and verify the value is *FRCSIGNON. Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QRMTSIGN) VALUE('*FRCSIGNON')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to *FRCSIGNON: QRMTSIGN CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QRMTSIGN) VALUE('*FRCSIGNON')

title: Set System Security Level
description: Determines the level of security features supported. Level 40 is the recommend level of security for non-DoD production systems. In addition to password authentication and privileged access controls, level 40 can effectively safeguard data, programs, and other production objects and prevent unintentional data loss or modification.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.23 Set System Security Level

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSECURITY) (or WRKSYSVAL QSECURITY) and verify the value is "50". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSECURITY) VALUE('50')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "50": QSECURITY CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSECURITY) VALUE('50')

title: Set Shared Memory Control
description: The Share Memory Control (QSHRMEMCTL) system value defines which users are allowed to use shared memory or mapped memory that has write capability. Your environment may contain applications, each running different jobs, but sharing pointers within these applications.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.24 Set Shared Memory Control

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSHRMEMCTL) (or WRKSYSVAL QSHRMEMCTL) and verify the value is "0". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSHRMEMCTL) VALUE('0')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following value to "0": QSHRMEMCTL CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QSHRMEMCTL) VALUE('0')

title: Set Verify Object On Restore
description: Determines when signatures will be verified and if the object will be restored without a valid signature. (See also QALWOBJRST & QFRCCVNRST, 2.1.2.1 and 2.1.2.10) You can prevent anyone from restoring an object, unless that object has a correct digital signature from a trusted software provider.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2.25 Set Verify Object On Restore

audit.command: Run DSPSYSVAL SYSVAL(QVFYOBJRST) (or WRKSYSVAL QVFYOBJRST) and verify the value is "5". Remediate with: CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QVFYOBJRST) VALUE('5')

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, set the following system value to "5": QVFYOBJRST CHGSYSVAL SYSVAL(QVFYOBJRST) VALUE('5')

title: Network Attribute JOBACN (Network Job Action)
description: The JOBACN network attribute determines how the system processes incoming requests to run jobs. The values for JOBACN are: *FILE: The input stream is filed in the queue of network files for the recipient. An authorized user may then view, delete, receive, or submit the job stream. Incoming job streams from remote systems do not authenticate remote credentials (passwords) and thus present an unauthenticated access vulnerability.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.1 Network Attribute JOBACN (Network Job Action)

audit.command: On a command line, type STRSQL and press Enter Copy or type the following SQL statement to the terminal and press Enter. SELECT JOB_ACTION FROM QSYS2/NET_ATTR Verify that the value for Job action is set to *REJECT.

remediation.command: To establish the recommended configuration, change the Network Attribute JOBACN to *REJECT: CHGNETA JOBACN(*REJECT)

title: DDM Remote Configuration List (SNA) Attributes
description: The Secure Location (SECURELOC) defines how security information is handled for program start requests received from remote system. Setting SECURELOC to a value of *NO specifies that the local system is not a secure system. All DDM Remote Configuration List entries shall specify *VFYENCPWD for the Secure Location (SECURELOC) parameter.
reference: CIS IBM i V7R5M0 Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.2 DDM Remote Configuration List (SNA) Attributes

audit.command: DSPCFGL CFGL(QAPPNRMT) -Note that if you receive the message "Configuration list QAPPNRMT not found", this indicates that your system is not configured for DDM over SNA and this setting is irrelevant. Ensure that all Secure Loc parameters = *VFYENCPWD.
